summary: André Godard worked in archaeology, history, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the École nationale supérieure des beaux-arts (~1899–1909) and held a post at the University of Tehran (~1934–1953).

Linguist André Martinet studied at the Sorbonne (~1928–1937), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1931–1932), and under Antoine Meillet (~1930–1936). He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1938–1993), Columbia University (~1947–1955), and the University of Paris (~1955–1978).
Linguist André Mazon studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1899–1902) and Charles University (~1902–1905). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1923 to 1951.

André Padoux worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the Institut de civilisation indienne, under Georg Morgenstierne, Alf Sommerfelt, Swami Lakshman Joo, Lilian Silburn, and doctoral supervisors Olivier Lacombe and Louis Renou. He held posts at Institut Français Frankfurt and CNRS.
Working in Sinology, Japanology, and linguistics, André Wedemeyer completed his doctoral studies under August Conrady. He later held a post at the University of Leipzig.

Andy Rotman specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock and Steven Collins, among others. He held posts at Smith College and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Angela Falco Howard works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She studied at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and Yoshito S. Hakeda, and held a professorship at Rutgers University (attested 2005).
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. She held posts at the Free University of Berlin and the University of Oulu (attested 1998).

Angela Sumegi specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa, studying under Nalini Devdas, and served as an assistant professor at Carleton University (attested 2008).
Angela Zito works in religious studies and Sinology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago in 1989 and held an associate professorship at New York University (~2001).

Philosopher Angelika Krebs studied at Freiburg, New College, Konstanz, UC Berkeley, and Goethe University Frankfurt, completing her doctorate under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt, Basel, and visiting fellowships at Princeton and Munich.

Angelika Malinar specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz and the University of Tübingen (PhD and Habilitation). Her academic posts include Free University of Berlin, SOAS University of London, and University of Zurich.
Angelo Brelich worked in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Erzsébet University (~1931–1937) and held a post at Sapienza University of Rome (~1958–1977).

Angelo De Gubernatis specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Turin and Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890).
Anil Kumar works in computational fields, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Hyderabad in 2012 and also held a post there.

Anil Vidyalankar works in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi, and served as director of Sandhaan (attested 1999).

Anirban Dash works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as a research assistant (attested 2003–2005) and associate professor of Sanskrit (attested 2026).
Ankita Chakraborty is an Indology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami. She holds a post as a research scholar/fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Ankur Barua works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Sikkim Manipal University, and the University of Hong Kong under Dorothy C. Wong, and held a post at the University of Delhi (attested 2012).

Ann Appleby Hazlewood worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed a Master of Arts at the Australian National University under the supervision of Tissa Rajapatirana and Luise Hercus (attested 1983).
